name: AL-01
label: Likely R

key_factors: District's strong Republican lean (R+17 PVI) after redistricting
Jerry Carl's large fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Clyde Jones Jr.
Prediction markets price Democrats at just 3%
Open seat with no incumbent and no general-election polling
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Carl's overwhelming financial edge, and a 95% Republican market price all point to a comfortable Republican win; I stay essentially at the baseline of -16.4 with no evidence to move away.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending surge for Jones could shift the margin, though a Democratic upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and its fundamentals strongly favor Republicans, with a partisan lean of about R+17. Jerry Carl, the better-funded Republican, has raised over $1.1 million and benefits from more than $500,000 in outside support, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $90,000 with no outside help.

With no public polling and no expert ratings, the forecast rests on fundamentals, money, and prediction markets, which give Democrats only a 3% chance. The expected Republican margin is roughly 16 points, consistent with the district's lean and the resource imbalance.
